source: The Agriculture Magazine (ទស្សនាវដ្តីកសិកម្ម), Issue 247, Quarter 3, 2013, poster page 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះ ពោត (១)' (Cultivation Technique: Corn, Part 1) — land preparation and planting section; credited to TSTD-TA 735-CAM project
text:
Corn cultivation begins with plowing and harrowing the field (ការភ្ជួររាស់ដី) to loosen the soil, followed by measuring out the planting layout (វាស់វែងទីតាំងសាបព្រោះ) and forming raised ridges/rows (កម្លស់រង). The poster labels a ridge cross-section with a height/width measurement of 0.3-0.5m. After ridging, organic fertilizer is applied as a basal (bottom) dressing in the planting furrow before sowing (ការដាក់ជីសរីរាង្គ ទ្រាប់បាត), and the furrow is then covered over the seed/fertilizer to help suppress weeds (គ្របំបើងដីម្បីកាត់បន្ថយស្មៅ).

Two row-spacing layouts are diagrammed side by side. Layout 1: row width (ទទឹងរង) of 1m planted with two rows of corn per bed, with plant-to-plant spacing within each row of 0.35-0.4m and 0.5m between the two paired rows — labeled 'ទទឹងរង១ម៉ែត្រ ដាំពីរជួរ' (row width 1m, plant two rows). Layout 2: row width of 0.5m planted with a single row per bed, with plant-to-plant spacing of 0.35-0.5m and 0.5m between adjacent single-row beds — labeled 'ទទឹងរង 0.5ម៉ែត្រ ដាំ១ជួរ' (row width 0.5m, plant one row).

For planting, a fertilizer/planting hole is dug roughly 10cm from the seedling position (labeled '10cm' with an arrow in the poster's planting diagram), placing holes at the center point of each plant clump so fertilizer can be worked in without directly touching the seed.
